en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province is famous for its nearly perfect conical shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Philippine tarsier, native to Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates and has enormous eyes adapted for night vision.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Babuyan Channel.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the largest lake in the region and the second-largest freshwater lake in the Philippines.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its pristine coral atolls.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 symmetrical grass-covered mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Baguio City in the Cordillera region experiences a subtropical climate, making it significantly cooler than most of the Philippines.
The Banaue Rice Terraces in Ifugao province were carved into the mountains by indigenous people over 2,000 years ago.
Rafflesia schadenbergiana, found in Mount Kitanglad, is a rare parasitic plant that produces the largest individual flower in the Philippines.
The Philippine Trench is a deep oceanic trench extending over 1,300 kilometers along the eastern seaboard of the Philippine archipelago.
